headline: France unrest markets appear; oil cools as blockade-deal odds tick up
summary: Brand-new markets on curfews and a state of emergency in France opened overnight, which suggests serious unrest. Oil pulled back from last week's spike as odds of the US lifting the Iran blockade rose. Large traders put about $126k on the Fed holding in October and about $175k on Anthropic surviving, and Anthropic's IPO timing odds jumped.

takeaways.text: New since yesterday: a Paris curfew by Oct 21 is 26% (up 21 pts in a day), and a curfew in any major French city by Oct 31 is 53%. A national state of emergency by year-end is 15.5%, and martial law is 3.4%. These are all thin markets ($24k–$111k), but new markets like these usually mean something is happening on the ground. Watch French stocks and the euro.

WTI hitting $100 this month fell 9 pts to 78% (still up 37 this week). $105 is 40% (down 6) and $110 is 17% (down 6). The US ending the Iran blockade by year-end rose 5 pts to 39.4%, and by Nov 30 rose 5 to 24%. A trader also bet $13k that oil won't hit $120.

takeaways.lead: $126k bet that the Fed holds in October.
takeaways.text: No change on Oct 29 rose to 88.5% (up 5 pts this week), backed by three large orders of $35–48k. A December hike is still 76.5%.

takeaways.lead: Anthropic's IPO clock is speeding up.
takeaways.text: An IPO by Nov 30 rose 6 pts to 61.5%, by Dec 15 rose 8 to 74.5%, and by Nov 15 rose 9 to 13.4%. About $175k of large bets went on Anthropic NOT going bankrupt by 2027–28, and $36k on an IPO by Nov 30 or Dec 31.

takeaways.lead: US politics: an 'election emergency' bet is rising.
takeaways.text: Trump declaring an election-interference national emergency by Dec 31 jumped 10 pts to 30.5% (thin $208k market), two weeks before the midterms. Defense Secretary Hegseth out by year-end is 29.5% (up 11 this week).

takeaways.lead: Brazil swung back toward Lula despite the whales.
takeaways.text: Bolsonaro fell 4 pts to 77%, and Lula rose 3 to 22.5%, even though another $104k of large bets went on Bolsonaro today. The runoff is Sunday, Oct 25.

sections.title: What's new today
bullets: France: four new markets on curfews, a state of emergency and martial law (see takeaways). All are thin, so they are early warnings only.
The next White House press secretary market has grown to $450k: an announcement by Nov 30 is 52.5% (down 7). Anna Kelly and Scott Jennings are tied at 14%.
Netanyahu as the next world leader out of power before 2027 rose 6 pts to 35% (up 11 this week).

sections.title: Trading signals
bullets: Oil: WTI $100 in October 78% (down 9 today), $105 40%, $110 17%. Blockade-relief odds are rising, so watch for a sharper drop if a deal headline hits.
Fed: October hold 88.5%, December hike 76.5%. No rate relief this year.
Largest company at the end of October: Nvidia 88% (up 10 pts), Apple 11% (down 11). Apple's run at the top has faded for now.
Bitcoin: large bets keep saying it won't dip to $65k in October.

sections.title: Wars & geopolitics
bullets: Israel–Iran ceasefire through Oct 31: 87.5% (up 2); through Dec 31: 48.5% (down 8 this week). Near-term calm, but the longer-term risk is rising again.
About $69k of large bets went on the Israel–Iran and US–Iran ceasefires holding through Oct 18.
A Saudi–Houthi ceasefire by year-end fell back 9 pts to 23.5% (thin market), undoing yesterday's optimism.

sections.title: Elections that move markets
bullets: Brazil (Oct 25): Bolsonaro 77%, Lula 22.5%. The margin market still says a race decided by under 4 points is most likely.
Israel (Oct 27): Eizenkot 48% (down 5 today), Netanyahu 28.5%. Likud winning fewer than 20 seats rose 6 pts to 31.5%.
France 2027: large traders bet against Philippe ($20k) and Lisnard ($16k) winning. Le Pen is still the favorite.

sections.title: Everyday life
bullets: Gas: oil is cooling a little, but $100 this month is still 78% likely, so don't expect relief at the pump yet.
Travel to France: curfew odds are rising. Check advisories if you have a trip planned in the next two weeks.
Borrowing costs: a December Fed hike is 76.5% likely, so variable-rate loans and credit cards may edge up.
